Anna L: ran the new SM-capability probe on the A100 V5 cluster this morning. weird perf cliff around seqlen 64->128, overall throughput drops ~22% for the fp8 path
Jordan: can you paste the probe dump? which flags fired?
Anna L: sure, raw output below (trimmed). noticed `tensor_core_fp8=1` but `sm_version=89` reported unexpectedly on some nodes
```
> probe: gpu0: sm=89 driver=525.60 tensor_cores=1 bf16=1 fp8=1
> microbench: seqlen=32: 12.4 tokens/s, seqlen=64: 9.8 tokens/s, seqlen=128: 7.6 tokens/s
> kernel_choice: fastpath_fp8_kv -> selected
> fallback log: none
```
Kai: hmm if sm reported 89 we pick FP8 kernel which expects TC-accelerated GEMMs. older cuda driver/hw quirk might misadvertise fp8 support even though kernel perf regresses
perf-bot: regression detected: +22% latency at seqlen range [64,128] after kernel-route change (deploy 2487400000)
Jordan: did we enable the `prefer_fp8_fastpath` capflag in the runtime rollout? I remember a canary flip yesterday
Anna L: yes, canary flipped at 2487401200. I think detection + capflag combined to route traffic to FP8 kernels on devices that actually underperform due to driver math kernels
Kai: also seeing KV-cache thrash on those runs — the FP8 kernel's KV layout increased memory churn for mid-sized batches. seqlen gating should prefer the stable bf16 path for 64-128 on these cards
OpsBot: created ticket INF-1982 and pinned canary to previous rollout. link: https://tickets.redwood/INF-1982
Jordan: proposed quick mitigations: (1) add strict driver+sm-version whitelist before choosing fp8 fastpath, (2) temporary bias in sequence-length heuristics to favor bf16 for seqlen>=64 && seqlen<=128, (3) KV prefetch smoothing to avoid thrash
Anna L: wrote a small microbenchmark and a patched detector that cross-checks `fp8=1` with a microkernal sanity run. results: when microkernel fails, we mark device as `fp8_unreliable` for 30m
```
> sanity-run gpu0 fp8-test: conv_ok=false, gemm_err_margin=0.12
> mark: fp8_unreliable until 2487656120
```
Kai: can you open a PR for the detector + heuristic tweak? I can run a scaled job on the canary fleet. would like to measure tokens/sec and KV cache miss rate difference
Anna L: will open PR later today. temp rollback queued if scaled job shows >10% regression vs baseline. added test cases for seqlen 64/96/128 in the autotune harness
Jordan: nice. once PR lands, let's run 24h canary with tracing (token latency p95/p99 + kv-cache miss histograms). logging should include `kernel_path` + `detector_flags` per request to correlate
perf-bot: note: schedule perf-run 2487656000 -> 2487742400 (24h) once PR merges
Anna L: thanks all — main action items: PR for detector+heuristic (Anna), scaled canary run (Kai), ticket INF-1982 for postmortem (OpsBot). will update thread with perf numbers and the dashboard link
OpsBot: posted dashboard snapshot: https://dashboard.redwood/internal/perf/2487654321 (access: eng-runtime) :thumbsup:
